title: Thirty Years’ War
key_facts: Complex conflict involving religious and dynastic rivalries across Central Europe
Began with the Defenestration of Prague and Bohemian Revolt
Foreign interventions by Sweden and France shifted the balance
causes: Religious tensions between Protestant and Catholic states
Fragmented Holy Roman Empire and Habsburg consolidation efforts
Power politics among major European powers
outcome: Peace of Westphalia (1648) redefining sovereignty and non‑intervention
Massive demographic and economic devastation in German lands
Diminished Habsburg imperial influence; rise of France and Sweden
impacts: Foundational concepts of modern state sovereignty
Religious pluralism within the Holy Roman Empire
Long‑term political fragmentation of German territories
